newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds find renewed confidence.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds find renewed confidence.

text.p: Australian bonds staged a solid rebound after last week's heavy liquidation with yields ending near to this year's recent lows.

The market found renewed confidence after U.S. Treasuries rallied strongly on Friday and yields stayed near the lows after a mixed bag of data showed a weaker than expected 1.4 percent rise in retail trade for October.

"The consumer remains weak, despite pre-Christmas discounting. This is not surprising as household disposable income would be held down by weak employment growth and moderating wages growth," said economists at Societe Generale.

However, the market reaction to this subdued activity was offset by a sharp 12.8 percent jump in October building approvals and an unexpectedly strong 2.3 percent third quarter reading in stocks inventories.

The latter piece of data is now seen contributing 0.5 percent to third quarter GDP when expectations had been for a 0.4 percent detraction. This saw economists revise up their forecasts for Wednesday's GDP to 0.9 percent from 0.6 percent.
Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank board meets on Tuesday, but a recent Reuters poll of economists gave only a 10 percent chance of a monetary policy easing after the meeting.
The market sold off heavily last week following comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane who again warned about excessive wage demands fuelling inflation.
However, National Mutual Funds Management feels there has been too much focus put on the pace of wage inflation as an indicator for potential price inflation.

NMFM's chief economist Michael Bargholz said the two most important impulses for inflation are the rate of growth and movements in the exchange rate. The past 12 months have witnessed a weaker economy and a stronger Australian dollar, and he sees CPI inflation falling to 1.0 percent in the next year.

The firm tone saw spreads to other dollar bloc bonds squeezed back in after last week's steep underperformance. However, the market is finding resistance in pushing back below 100 basis points on the 10-year bond yield spread to the U.S.. U.S. bonds gave up some of Friday's gains in Tokyo trading.
The 10-year bond contract is now pressing stiff resistance in the mid-92.900s after making a solid rebound from 92.760 last Friday. Immediate target remains recent 33-month high at 92.995.
